title: Escaped wildcard glob matching
instructions:
Implement `GlobPattern` and `glob_match` in `glob_matcher.py`. This is a whole-string, case-sensitive matcher, not a filesystem search:
- `GlobPattern(pattern)` parses a string pattern. Unescaped `?` matches exactly one Python character; unescaped `*` matches zero or more characters. They match everything including slashes and newlines. A backslash escapes the next character, making it literal (including `*`, `?`, or backslash). A trailing backslash raises `ValueError` at construction. All other characters, including square brackets, dots and parentheses, are literal. Empty patterns are valid. Consecutive stars are equivalent to one star.
- `matches(text) -> bool`: True exactly when the entire text matches. Repeated calls are independent.
- `filter(strings) -> list[str]`: consume an iterable and return matching strings in their input order, retaining duplicates.
- `glob_match(pattern, text) -> bool`: convenience function with the same pattern validation and matching behavior.
Use a polynomial-time algorithm (e.g. dynamic programming), not exponential recursive backtracking. Patterns/texts up to 300 characters must be practical; no regex translation is necessary. Python Unicode code points count as characters.

## Files
- `glob_matcher.py`
